PUBLIC COMMENT
Citizens wishing to address the City Council and Successor Agency on any item on the agenda or on any matter
not on the agenda may do so at this time. State law (Government Code Section 54950 et seq.) prohibits the City
Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda .
Upon request, the City Council may, in their discretion, allow citizen participation on a specific item on the agenda
at the time the item is considered by the City Council. If you wish to address the City Council /Successor Agency
at this time, please complete a speaker's card and give it to the City Clerk prior to commencement of the City
Council meeting. Please limit your remarks to three (3) minutes.

To increase the effectiveness of the Public Comment Period, the following rules shall be followed: No person shall
make any remarks which result in disrupting, disturbing or otherwise impeding the meeting.

Pursuant to Section 54957.95 of the Government Code, the presiding member of the legislative body conducting a
meeting, or their designee, is authorized to remove, or cause the removal of, an individual for disrupting the
meeting. Any such removal will be preceded by a warning to the disruptive individual by the presiding member of
the legislative body or their designee that the individual ’s behavior is disrupting the meeting and that the individual ’s
failure to promptly cease their disruptive behavior may result in their removal.

  CONSENT CALENDAR
Items under the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine and may be enacted by one motion. There will be
no discussion of these items unless members of the Public or City Council request specific items to be removed
from the Consent Agenda for a separate discussion. lf the item is desired to be discussed separately, it should be
the first item under Scheduled Matters.

  Park
  The City Council will receive and file the conceptual rendering for the

  The City Council will receive and file City staff's presentation regarding the
  establishment of a pilot program entitled the Walls of Freedom public art
  project in the Bristow Park area and provide a direction to staff as may be
  deemed necessary.
  Attachments:  Staff report

  The City Council will review the submitted artwork and consider selecting
  artwork from the following artists: Daniel Antelo, Jerome Castro, Ruben Rojas,
  Nerv, and Alejandro "Man One" Poli Jr.
  Attachments:  Staff Report

  PUBLIC HEARING

10.  Extension of a Citywide Moratorium Prohibiting the Approval, Expansion,
  Intensification or Relocation of Any New or Existing Home-Sharing for a
  period of Ten (10) Months and Fifteen (15) Days -Public Hearing
  The City Council will consider approving an extension of Interim Urgency
  Ordinance No. 821, continuing a temporary moratorium on the approval,
  expansion, intensification, or relocation of any new or existing home-sharing or
  vacation rental operations within the City of Commerce for an additional ten
  (10) months and fifteen (15) days, in accordance with California Government
  Code Section 65858, to June 28, 2026.
  Attachments:  Staff Report
  Interim Urgency Ordinance

AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
5:00 P.M. CLOSED SESSION

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Ivan Altamirano called meeting to order at 5:12 P.M.

ROLL CALL Councilmember Rebollo was not present for roll call, but joined the Closed Session meeting.

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION ITEMS There were no individuals wishing to address the City Council on any Closed Session items.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION The members of the City Council and Successor Agency recessed to Closed Session at 5:14 p.m.

RECONVENE TO OPEN SESSION The members of the City Council and Successor Agency reconvened to open session at 6:28 p.m.

ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT City Attorney Tapia reported on Closed Session Item No. 1, stating that with the entire Council present, four potential litigation matters were discussed. Staff provided a presentation, the City Council gave direction, and no reportable action was taken on any of the items.

6:00 P.M. - CITY COUNCIL MEETING

ROLL CALL

City Clerk Lena Shumway announced that there were no public comments received for the Public Hearing.

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Councilmember Oralia Rebollo
1. Veterans Park: Apologized to the community and is committed to holding herself accountable to the promises made regarding the project. Thanked staff for working with what they have and will commit to the park's maintenance, the project's progress, and ensuring the community's quality of life is at the forefront of every decision for that park. 

Councilmember Mireya Garcia
1. Veterans Park: Apologized for the condition of Veterans Park and stated that Council is working diligently to improve it.
2.. Discover the Art & Culture of El Salvador event at the Rosewood library: Thanked the staff for their hard work for the event and requested to be in contact with the artists that were on display. 

Councilmember Hugo Argumedo:
1. Veterans Park: Provided updates on project and stated that the objective is to have a beautiful, state-of-the-art facility and a new park. Also mentioned a goal to establish a temporary location as soon as possible. 
2. Fiestas Patrias event: Thanked the Parks and Recreation Department and organization staff for the event.

Mayor Pro Tem Kevin Lainez:
1. Veterans Park: Apologized for the state of Veterans Park and acknowledged concerns raised by the community. He stated that solutions are actively being sought for the promised facility. Emphasized that the park should be maintained like other City parks.
2. Homeless activity at alley along Jillson St. and Washington: Acknowledged the numerous complaints received from residents detailing the increased homeless activity overnight, illegal dumping, and safety issues. Requested more patrol and monitoring to the area.
3. Fiestas Patrias event: Thanked the Public Works, Public Safety, Library, Transportation, and Parks and Recreation Departments for their excellent work on the event. 
4. Discover the Art & Culture of El Salvador event at the Rosewood library: Congratulated the library staff for the wonderful event, noting the great turnout and the successful collaboration with La Asociación de Salvadoreños en Los Angeles.
5. Reminded the community of the Commerce to College Fair and the grand opening of the Bandini Library. 

Mayor Ivan Altamirano had no comments.  


ADJOURNMENT Mayor Ivan Altamirano adjourned the meeting at 8:08 p.m.
